study_identification_part.si_4_title: Transdiagnostic dimensions of psychopathology explain individuals' unique deviations from normative neurodevelopment in brain structure

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: The study exclusively uses the Philadelphia Neurodevelopmental Cohort (PNC), a large community-based study of brain development in youths aged 8-22 years. All scanning was done using the same sequences on the same scanner (3T Siemens Tim Trio) at the Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania. From the original 1,601 PNC participants, 1,271 were retained after exclusions for radiological abnormalities, quality assurance failures, missing demographics, and familial links.

answer.PNC: normative model training (281 HC), normative model testing and clinical application (990 individuals: 100 HC + 890 with psychopathology)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The PNC sample (n=1,271) was split into two subsets based on psychiatric history: (1) a normative training subset of 281 healthy individuals (no clinically significant symptoms) used to train Gaussian process regression models of cortical volume as a function of age and sex; (2) a testing subset of 990 individuals (100 randomly sampled healthy individuals combined with 890 individuals with psychopathology) used for computing z-score deviations and predicting psychopathology dimensions. Additionally, 10-fold cross-validation was performed within the training subset to generate deviations for those 281 individuals.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: "A total of 381 individuals reported no clinically significant symptoms on any disorder examined, while 890 individuals reported experiencing psychopathology. Next, ... we randomly sampled 100 of the 381 healthy individuals and combined them with the aforementioned 890 individuals to create a testing subset totaling 990 individuals. The remaining 281 healthy individuals were designated as our normative training subset."

model-1.model-name: GPR normative model of cortical volume

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: A single normative model was constructed using Gaussian process regression (GPR) to predict regional cortical volume from age and sex. The total healthy control pool was 381 individuals (no clinically significant symptoms). Of these, 281 were designated as the normative training subset, while 100 were randomly sampled and placed into the testing subset (990 total). Within the training subset, 10-fold cross-validation was also performed to generate deviations for the 281 training individuals.

The overall HC pool (n=381) age statistics are not reported separately; the 100 HC randomly sampled into the test set are not described independently. Min/max are inferred from the stated PNC age range of 8-22 years. The full sample (n=1,271) had mean age 15.10 (SD 3.64).
